title: Cursor Pricing in 2026: Plans, Credits, and Cost Breakdown
summary: Explore Cursor pricing in 2026, including plans, credits, usage-based billing, overages, and the added cost of deploying and running your app.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


## Key takeaways


-


Cursor offers a free Hobby plan, while paid individual plans cost $20, $60, or $200 per month.


-


Paid plans include metered first-party and third-party usage allowances, and consumption depends on the models, tokens, and context used.


-


Auto consumes included usage under current plans, while Max Mode can drain the allowance faster through larger context windows.


-


Cursor covers AI-assisted coding but not the hosting, database, authentication, or monitoring required to operate an app.


-


Modelence combines app building with managed production infrastructure, although container runtime is billed separately.


Ask AI about this post:


Cursor pricing starts at a clean $20 per month, but the subscription price is only part of the real cost.


It uses a usage-based credit system with separate first-party and third-party usage pools. What you ultimately pay depends on which models you use, how often you run agents, and whether you enable overage billing.


This guide makes two things clear that Cursor’s pricing page does not: what actually drains your credits, and why Cursor’s price covers writing code but not hosting, deploying, or running what you build.


It also breaks down every Cursor AI pricing plan, its included usage, and what happens when your allowances run out.


## **Cursor Pricing Overview**


Cursor offers a free plan, three paid individual tiers, two team seat types, and a custom Enterprise plan.


**Plan** **Monthly** **Annual Billing** **Included Usage** **Tab Completions** **Best For **


**Hobby** Free Free Limited Agent requests Limited Trying Cursor


**Pro** $20/month $16/month $20 of guaranteed third-party API usage, plus a separate first-party models pool Unlimited Solo developers


**Pro+** $60/month $48/month $70 of guaranteed third-party API usage, plus a separate first-party models pool Unlimited Daily Agent users


**Ultra** $200/month $160/month $400 of guaranteed third-party API usage, plus a separate first-party models pool Unlimited Power users running Agents heavily


**Teams Standard** $40/user/month $32/user/month Included first-party and third-party model usage Unlimited Collaborative development teams


**Teams Premium** $120/user/month $96/user/month Five times the included usage of Standard Unlimited Teams with heavy Agent users


**Enterprise** Custom Custom Pooled usage Unlimited Larger organizations needing advanced controls


Above Pro, individual plans mainly provide more model usage rather than a different editor experience.


Pro+ targets daily Agent users, while Ultra is designed for developers running several Agents or automations heavily.


Annual billing reduces self-service prices by 20%.


Teams Premium was announced in June 2026 and provides five times the total included usage of Standard.


The new structure applied immediately to new customers and applies to existing customers when their billing cycle renews on or after July 1, 2026. Companies can mix Standard and Premium seats; taxes and pay-as-you-go usage may increase the final cost.


The Cursor prices and plan details above were verified in July 2026.


## **What You Get With Each Cursor Pricing Plan**


Cursor’s paid individual plans share most of the same features. Moving above Pro mainly buys more model usage rather than a different coding environment.


### **Hobby: Best for Trying Cursor**


Hobby is free and includes limited Agent requests and Tab completions, with no credit card required.


It works as an extended trial for testing Cursor on small tasks. Regular coding or Agent use will quickly require a paid plan.


### **Pro: Best for Solo Developers**


Pro costs **$20 per month** or **$16 per month billed annually** .


It includes:


- Unlimited Tab completions
- Extended Agent limits
- Access to frontier models
- Cloud agents
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, skills, and hooks
- $20 of guaranteed third-party API usage, plus a separate first-party models pool


Pro fits solo developers who use Tab regularly and Agent moderately.


The amount of work it covers depends heavily on the models selected because premium models consume the usage pool at different rates.


### **Pro+ and Ultra: Best for Heavy Agent Use**


Pro+ costs **$60 per month** and includes **$70 of guaranteed third-party API usage** , plus a separate first-party models pool. Ultra costs **$200 per month** and includes **$400 of guaranteed third-party API usage** , plus a separate first-party models pool and priority access to new features.


Both plans otherwise provide largely the same core tools as Pro. Their value comes from purchasing a larger usage allowance:


- **Pro+** suits developers who use Agent daily and regularly exceed Pro’s limits.
- **Ultra** suits power users running several agents, automations, or large coding tasks throughout the day.


Cursor estimates that daily Agent users often consume $60 to $100 of monthly usage, while heavy users running multiple agents may exceed $200.


### **Teams and Enterprise: Best for Organizations**


Teams Standard costs **$40 per user per month** or **$32 with annual billing** . It adds organizational features such as:


- Centralized billing and administration
- Team-wide privacy controls
- Usage analytics
- Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) or OpenID Connect (OIDC) single sign-on
- Shared context for cloud agents and automations
- Internal marketplaces for rules, skills, and plugins


Teams Premium costs **$120 per user monthly** or **$96 with annual billing** and includes five times the usage of Standard.


Companies can mix Standard and Premium seats, allowing heavier Agent users to receive larger allowances without upgrading everyone.


Enterprise uses custom pricing and adds pooled usage, System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), audit logs, repository and model controls, invoice billing, networking controls, and priority support.


Individual developers rarely need Teams or Enterprise unless collaboration, centralized governance, or formal security requirements matter more than the additional seat cost.


## **How Does Cursor’s Credit System Work?**


Cursor’s current individual plans provide two separate usage pools:


- **First-party models pool:** Included usage for Auto, Composer 2.5, and Cursor Grok 4.5. Cursor does not publish this pool as a fixed dollar amount, but it grows with each plan tier.
- **Third-party API pool:** Pro includes $20, Pro+ includes $70, and Ultra includes $400 of guaranteed API usage for models such as Claude, GPT, and Gemini.


First-party models draw from the first-party pool first. Once that allowance is exhausted, additional first-party usage can draw from the included API pool. Paid on-demand billing begins only after the included pools are exhausted and when on-demand usage is enabled.


### **Auto Mode Also Uses Your Allowance**


Under Cursor’s current pricing, Auto draws from the included first-party models pool at these fixed token rates. Once that pool is exhausted, additional Auto usage can draw from the included API allowance.


- **Cached input:** $0.25 per million tokens
- **Input:** $1.25 per million tokens
- **Output:** $6 per million tokens


Accounts on older annual subscriptions may temporarily retain legacy terms until renewal, but current plans meter Auto as part of the included allowance.


The usage allowances and token rates above were verified in July 2026.


Manually selected frontier models are charged at their providers’ API rates.


Max Mode can cost more because it supports longer reasoning and context windows of up to one million tokens. It is useful for large codebases and complex tasks, but unnecessary use can drain credits much faster.


### **How Quickly Cursor’s Included Usage Can Run Out**


The amount of work covered depends on the model and task. The request estimates for Claude, Gemini, and GPT apply to the third-party API pool, while Auto draws from the separate first-party models pool first.


**Model or Mode** **Approximate Usage Within Pro** **Usage Pool Used**


**Auto** No fixed request count; charged by tokens First-party models pool first


**Claude Sonnet 4** About 225 requests Third-party API pool


**Gemini** About 550 requests Third-party API pool


**GPT-5** About 500 requests Third-party API pool


**Max Mode** Varies widely and can consume substantially more Depends on the selected model


These figures are estimates, not guaranteed request limits.


A short question may cost very little, while a large refactor involving several files and a long conversation can use far more tokens.


### **What Happens When Credits Run Out?**


Cursor notifies you in the editor when you reach the included monthly allowance. You can then:


- Purchase additional usage at API cost
- Upgrade to Pro+ or Ultra
- Wait for the allowance to reset during the next billing cycle


Additional usage does not automatically reduce model quality or speed.


Builders who enable on-demand billing should set a spending limit rather than leaving it unrestricted, since usage can continue beyond the subscription price.


The practical risk is that a busy development week can cost more than a quiet one.


Monitor the usage dashboard, keep conversations focused, and reserve expensive models or Max Mode for tasks that genuinely require them.


## **Cursor’s 2025 Pricing Overhaul and the Backlash It Caused**


In June 2025, Cursor replaced Pro’s 500 fast requests with a $20 usage pool billed at model API rates.


Complex requests could now consume far more than simple ones, but the rollout did not make that change clear.


Users reported unexpected charges of $10 to $20 per day, while one team said its $7,000 annual plan was depleted in a single day during the[pricing backlash](https://www.wearefounders.uk/cursors-pricing-disaster-the-full-timeline-of-how-an-ai-coding-darling-burned-its-most-loyal-users/) .


Cursor’s CEO apologized, and the company issued refunds, clarified its pricing, and improved spending controls and usage visibility.


However, it did not restore the old request-based plan.


The credit model remains in place in 2026, which is why power users still watch their usage meters and overage limits closely.


Before subscribing, buyers should understand that Cursor’s monthly price does not guarantee a fixed amount of Agent work.


## **General Developer Sentiment About Cursor Pricing**


Developer sentiment about Cursor pricing is mixed.


Many users still value the productivity gains, but complaints tend to focus on unclear consumption and allowances running out faster than expected.


-


**The $20 plan can still provide good value:** Some developers find Auto and Composer useful at the base price, although the value depends heavily on avoiding expensive models and overages.


-


**Opaque usage causes more frustration than the price itself:** In[Cursor’s pricing forum](https://forum.cursor.com/t/pricing-megathread-and-q-a/116395) , one user summarized the concern plainly: “I can accept the price increase, but I can’t accept opaque consumption.” Users repeatedly asked for clearer model costs and remaining-usage information.


-


**Heavy frontier-model use can drain even larger plans:** Users reported exhausting Ultra quickly when relying heavily on Claude Opus, Sonnet, or other high-cost models, leading some to combine Cursor with separate coding-tool subscriptions.


-


**Unexpected overages make developers monitor every session:** One developer reported[spending $131 in a month](https://hackernoon.com/cursors-new-pricing-blew-my-budget-so-i-built-a-usage-tracker) after the pricing change—about seven times the previous month—and built a usage tracker to understand where the money went. This is an individual experience, not a typical-cost benchmark.


-


**Some developers still consider the cost worthwhile:** Hacker News discussions include users who view AI coding costs as justified when maintaining context saves meaningful development time, even while acknowledging that heavy usage becomes expensive.


The overall pattern is not that Cursor is universally considered too expensive.


Users mainly want clearer visibility into what each model and Agent session will cost before their credits are consumed.


## **The Cost Cursor’s Pricing Doesn’t Show: Shipping to Production**


Cursor’s subscription covers AI-assisted coding, not the full cost of running what you build.


A production app may still need:


- Hosting and deployment
- A backend and database
- Authentication and user roles
- File storage and email services
- Logs, monitoring, and backups
- Domains, Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), and infrastructure maintenance


These services usually come from separate providers, each with its own pricing and setup.


Cursor’s $20 Pro plan can therefore speed up development without representing the total cost of shipping and operating the finished app.


Modelence approaches the problem differently by combining its AI App Builder with authentication, a database, monitoring, and managed deployment.


Starter costs $20 per month and includes one production instance, while the containers running the app are billed separately according to their size and runtime.


The two products solve different problems.


Cursor is a strong fit when you want a faster coding editor and prefer choosing your own infrastructure. Modelence fits builders who want the app and its production stack connected in one platform.

With Cursor, the subscription covers AI-assisted coding, while hosting, databases, authentication, monitoring, and deployment must be sourced separately.


Modelence includes those production tools and a set number of production instances, although container runtime is billed according to usage.

The Cursor price and usage details in the comparison above were verified in July 2026.


Cursor may cost less when you already have infrastructure and only need a faster coding editor.


Modelence may simplify launching a new full-stack application by reducing the number of separate services you need, but its subscription is not the complete hosting bill because container runtime is charged separately.


## **Is Cursor Worth It, and When Modelence Fits Better**


Cursor is worth the price when you want AI assistance inside a familiar coding workflow and already know how you will host, secure, and operate the finished application.


It offers strong value for developers who use Auto for routine work, reserve expensive models for harder tasks, and monitor their usage closely.


Modelence fits better when the goal is not only to write code but to launch a working full-stack product.


It connects the frontend, backend, database, authentication, monitoring, and managed deployment in one platform.


Choose **Cursor** when:


- You already have a development stack and infrastructure.
- You want more control over tools, frameworks, and cloud providers.
- Faster coding is the main priority.
- You are comfortable managing usage-based credits.


Choose **Modelence** when:


- You are starting a new full-stack application.
- You want the production stack connected from the beginning.
- You prefer separate visibility into building and runtime costs.
- You want to own and export the generated code.


The two tools are not mutually exclusive.


A developer may use Cursor to edit code while relying on Modelence or another platform to manage the application’s production infrastructure.


## **Build and Ship Fast With Modelence Without Billing Surprises**


Modelence separates App Builder usage from cloud runtime instead of making development and live-app activity draw from one shared balance.


Its Starter plan includes $20 in App Builder usage, one production instance, a managed database, and a custom domain.


Container runtime is billed separately according to the resources the app uses, so hosting is not unlimited, but development and production costs remain easier to distinguish.


Modelence also includes authentication, backend logic, monitoring, and deployment in the same workflow. You own the code and data and can export the project to GitHub or deploy it elsewhere.


You can[start building for free](https://modelence.com/platform) , validate the app, and move to a paid plan when it is ready for production.


## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)


How much does Cursor cost per month in 2026?


Cursor costs $0 for Hobby, $20 for Pro, $60 for Pro+, or $200 for Ultra, while Teams starts at $40 per user monthly.


Why did my Cursor credits run out so fast?


Credits can disappear quickly when you use expensive frontier models, Max Mode, long conversations, large codebases, or tasks that generate substantial input and output.


What’s the difference between Auto mode and Max Mode for billing?


Auto selects a model and consumes usage at Cursor’s Auto token rates, while Max Mode allows larger context and reasoning that generally costs more.


Does Cursor still offer the 500 fast requests plan?


No, the 500-request model is no longer Cursor’s standard plan because it was replaced by a dollar-value usage pool billed according to model consumption.


What happens when I hit my Cursor usage limit?


Cursor notifies you and lets you purchase additional usage at cost, upgrade your plan, or wait for the allowance to reset.


Is Cursor Pro or Ultra better value for heavy users?


Pro suits moderate Agent use, while Ultra provides much more included usage for developers who regularly run multiple agents, automations, or demanding tasks.


Does Cursor’s price include hosting or deploying my app?


No, Cursor’s subscription covers its coding tools and model usage, so production hosting and application infrastructure must be purchased or managed separately.


What’s a good Cursor alternative if I want predictable costs?


Modelence may fit builders who want app development and managed production tools in one platform, with App Builder and runtime costs tracked separately.
